question: Which of the following is the most accurate statement distinguishing a medico-legal (ML) autopsy from a clinical/hospital autopsy?

answers.text: A clinical autopsy requires written consent from the next of kin, whereas a medico-legal autopsy is conducted on the authority of law without such consent.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The medico-legal autopsy derives its authority from a statutory order (CRPC/police requisition) and does not require family consent; a clinical autopsy requires informed written consent.

answers.text: A medico-legal autopsy is conducted only for cases involving poisoning, whereas clinical autopsies cover all other deaths.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. ML autopsies cover all medico-legal deaths — unnatural, suspicious, unknown-cause — not just poisoning cases.

answers.text: A clinical autopsy is mandatory for all in-hospital deaths, while a medico-legal autopsy is optional.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Clinical autopsies are elective (consent-based); medico-legal autopsies are mandatory when legally required, not optional.

answers.text: Both clinical and medico-legal autopsies are ordered by the District Magistrate.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Only medico-legal autopsies may be ordered by a Magistrate; clinical autopsies are requested by treating physicians with family consent.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the distinction: clinical autopsies require consent and serve clinical audit; medico-legal autopsies operate under statutory authority (CRPC) irrespective of family consent.
Well done. Understanding the legal authority underpinning each type of autopsy is fundamental to your role as a forensic physician.
